data.raw_response:
=== Morphological Assessment Form ===
A. Leaf Arrangement & Architecture
    1. Leaf relative position (alternate / opposite / whorled): whorled (multiple leaves are clearly seen radiating from a single node in a circular pattern)
    2. Leaf spacing (clustered / distal): clustered (leaves are arranged in dense whorls at the stem tips)
B. Leaf Complexity
    3. Leaf complexity (simple / compound): simple (each leaf is a single blade without leaflets)
    4. Compound leaf type, ONLY if leaf complexity is compound (odd-pinnate / even-pinnate): N/A
    5. Number of leaflets (integer estimate 2, 4, 8, …): N/A
    6. Leaflet arrangement (opposite / alternate / subopposite): N/A
C. Leaf Morphology
    7. Leaf margin (entire / toothed) AND if toothed (dentate, serrate, etc.)): entire (leaf edges are smooth, though some show minor holes)
    8. Leaf shape (elliptic, obovate, lanceolate, etc.): lanceolate (leaves are long and narrow, tapering toward both ends)
    9. Leaf apex (acute, obtuse, acuminate): acute (the leaf tip tapers to a distinct point)
    10. Leaf base (rounded, cordate, cuneate): cuneate (the leaf narrows gradually to the petiole attachment)
    11. Venation type (pinnate / palmate / parallel): pinnate (a central midrib with secondary veins branching off)
    12. Secondary veins (visibility, spacing, number): clearly visible, prominent, and relatively evenly spaced
    13. Leaf surface features (glabrous, shiny, dull, rugose): shiny and rugose (the surface is glossy and has a textured, slightly bumpy appearance due to the venation)
    14. Leaf surface trichomes (present / absent): absent (the surface appears smooth and glabrous)
    15. Petiole length (short / long): short (the petioles are very short, causing the leaves to appear almost sessile at the whorl)
    16. Petiole features (winged / grooved / terete): terete (petioles appear cylindrical)
D. Stem & Shoot Traits
    17. Stem type, may not be visible (woody / herbaceous): herbaceous (the stems appear green, thin, and flexible)
    18. Stem trichomes (present / absent): absent (stems appear smooth)
    19. Stem color: green (with some darker, brownish tones further down the stem)
    20. Stem texture (smooth / ridged / lenticellate): smooth
E. Other Visible Seedling Traits
    21. Stipules, sometimes visible only in close-up images (present / absent): absent (no stipules are clearly visible at the leaf nodes)
    22. Latex, rarely visible but extremely diagnostic when present (present / not observed): not observed
    23. Pulvinus, for Fabaceae family only (present / absent): absent
    24. Tendrils (present / absent): absent
F. Notes: The seedling exhibits a distinct architectural pattern with leaves arranged in whorls. Several leaves show minor damage, specifically small holes in the margins and lamina.
